samples.summary: The new merge-map budget is enforced only on write paths; the load-time walk it exists to protect (`rebuildMergeCoverMap`) is still uncapped, so any principal with document write access can brick a tab via the CRDT
samples.evidence: All four new enforcement points are write-side and two of them are client code: `parseMerges` (backend `PUT merges`), `YorkieStore.setMerge` (browser), `Sheet.canMergeSelection`/`applyPasteMerges` (browser), and the XLSX importer (browser). Nothing validates merge-map *content* on the server for the collaborative path: `packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts` only answers the Yorkie auth webhook with (key, verb) allow/deny — it never inspects document ops. So a user who legitimately holds `rw` on a shared document (an invited editor, or a share-link editor) can attach with the Yorkie SDK, or a patched/older build of the frontend, and write `sheets[tab].merges = { A1: { rs: 1000000, cs: 18278 }, ... }` directly. `Sheet.loadMerges()` (sheet.ts:588) then calls `rebuildMergeCoverMap()` (sheet.ts:862), which loops `for r in rs { for c in cs { mergeCoverMap.set(...) } }` with no cap and no bail-out, on every collaborator's next open — including the workspace owner's. Result is a permanently unopenable tab: exactly the outcome `MaxMergedCells`'s own docstring calls "a document nobody can open again", and exactly what `docs/design/sheets/sheet.md` now asserts "cannot be created in the first place". The write-side caps raise the bar for the REST client while leaving the CRDT door open, and the new `mergeBudget` field is computed *after* the unbounded walk has already run, so it cannot stop it. Mitigation would be a cap at load (clamp/skip in `rebuildMergeCoverMap`/`loadMerges`) or server-side op validation, not only at the writers.
searchedFor: grep merges= / .merges across packages/backend/src (only parseMerges, migration, controllers)
grep for any backend Sheet instantiation that would validate loaded merges

samples.summary: `parseHidden` accepts unbounded-length `rows`/`columns` arrays — the same unbounded-collection DoS this change bounds for merges, left unbounded one function above it
samples.evidence: `parseHidden`'s inner `arr()` (worksheet-settings.ts:79-87) validates each element's range but never the array's length. `PUT /api/v1/.../tabs/:tabId/hidden` therefore accepts up to the full body-parser limit (`BACKEND_JSON_BODY_LIMIT`, default `25mb` — packages/backend/src/main.ts:20), i.e. roughly 3M integers, and `setHidden` writes them straight into the Yorkie root (`ws.hiddenRows = rows`, worksheet.controller.ts:174). That array is then part of the document every collaborator syncs and `Sheet.loadHiddenState` walks on open. This is the identical CWE-770 shape the diff just closed for `merges` (`mergeBudgetError` on entry count and covered cells), so a reviewer reading this file would reasonably assume the neighbouring writer is bounded too. Pre-existing, not introduced by the diff, but it is in a file this change edits and is the same class of stored resource-exhaustion.
searchedFor: grep JSON_BODY_LIMIT for the body cap
grep hiddenRows/hiddenColumns for a downstream length clamp

samples.summary: `mergeBudgetOf`/`mergeBudgetAdmits` compute over untrusted stored spans without numeric validation, so a single non-numeric span NaN-poisons the budget and every subsequent cap check silently passes
samples.evidence: `mergeBudgetOf` does `coveredCells += span.rs * span.cs` (merging.ts:58) over spans read from the document — `YorkieStore.setMerge` feeds it `projectedMerges()` (yorkie-store.ts:1014), the XLSX importer feeds it `Object.values(worksheet.merges)` (xlsx-importer.ts:250), and `Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap` computes `this.mergeBudget` the same way (sheet.ts:866). None of these validate that `rs`/`cs` are numbers. A stored span such as `{ rs: "x", cs: 1 }` — writable by any `rw` principal straight through the CRDT, since nothing validates document content server-side — makes `coveredCells` NaN; `mergeBudgetError` then evaluates `NaN > MaxMergeCoveredCells` as false and returns null, so `mergeBudgetAdmits` admits every subsequent block and `canMergeSelection` stops refusing. The per-span `cells > MaxMergedCells` guard is defeated the same way for the poisoned entry. The attacker needs CRDT write access, which already enables the larger issue above, so this is defence-in-depth erosion rather than a standalone exploit — but it turns the new cap into one that fails open on malformed input instead of failing closed.
searchedFor: grep mergeBudgetOf call sites (yorkie-store.ts, xlsx-importer.ts, sheet.ts)
checked parseMerges for rs/cs integer validation (present, API path only)

samples.summary: `PUT freeze` now stores a snapped boundary that can exceed the grid bound `parseFreeze` validates, bypassing the validator whose stated purpose is preventing an unpaintable, un-undoable document
samples.evidence: `parseFreeze` bounds `rows`/`cols` to `MaxRows`/`MaxColumns` and its docstring states the reason explicitly: an out-of-grid freeze "allocates per frame and the UI never paints — which also means the user cannot reach the freeze menu to undo it" (worksheet-settings.ts:50-57). The new code writes `snapped.frozenRows` (worksheet.controller.ts:126) instead of the validated `rows`, and `snapFreezePastMerges` grows the line to `anchor.r + rs - 1` of whatever merge it finds, with no re-clamp to the grid. Merges written through `parseMerges` are grid-clamped so this stays in bounds, but the XLSX importer is not: `applyMergeRanges` (xlsx-importer.ts:257-278) derives `rowSpan` from arbitrary refs in an attacker-supplied file and only checks the merge *budget*, never the grid, so an imported `A999000:A1048999` block (50,000 cells, inside `MaxMergedCells`) plus a legal `PUT freeze {rows: 1000000}` snaps the stored `frozenRows` to 1,048,999 — past the bound `parseFreeze` exists to enforce. The same uncapped snap now also runs unattended in `shiftWorksheetViewState` (worksheet-structure.ts:277) on every `POST insert`/`POST delete`. Marginal in practice (a 1e6 freeze is already unpaintable), so low confidence on real-world impact, but the snap should re-clamp to the grid rather than trusting the merge map.
searchedFor: read parseFreeze and its docstring in worksheet-settings.ts
read snapFreezePastMerges in merging.ts for a grid clamp
read applyMergeRanges in xlsx-importer.ts for a grid clamp
grep snapFreezePastMerges call sites (worksheet.controller.ts, worksheet-structure.ts, sheet.ts)

samples.summary: The freeze snap adds a per-call O(n log n) walk of the untrusted stored merge map to every backend insert/delete, inside a synchronous `doc.update`
samples.evidence: `shiftWorksheetViewState` now calls `snapFreezePastMerges` unconditionally (worksheet-structure.ts:276-282), which materializes one `Range` per merge (a `parseRef` each) and then, inside `sweep`, does `[...ranges].sort(...)` — twice, once per axis. On the backend this runs inside `doc.update` on an attached Yorkie document during `POST .../insert` and `POST .../delete` (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:355), i.e. synchronously on the Node event loop with nothing able to interrupt it. The merge map it walks is stored document state, and per the first finding its size is not bounded on the read side, so a large map (legacy, or written directly through the CRDT) turns every structural API call into an event-loop stall proportional to that map. The array copy and sort also run even when both freeze counts are 0, where the sweep immediately returns.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. `rebuildMergeCoverMap` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:862-877) walks rs*cs for every entry with no cap and no bail-out, and computes `mergeBudget` only at line 876, after the walk; `loadMerges` (sheet.ts:588-591) feeds it straight from the store and is invoked on every tab open (view/worksheet.ts:432). No read-side sanitizer exists: YorkieStore.getMerges (frontend yorkie-store.ts:1068-1076) copies entries verbatim through safeWorksheetRecordEntries, which only handles duplicate-own-key errors (sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-record.ts:47-61); memory.load (store/memory.ts:192-197) and cloneMergeRecord (backend worksheet-shape-migration.ts:86-96) also copy unvalidated. The server never inspects CRDT content: the Yorkie event webhook only touches updatedAt and explicitly notes content edits never traverse the backend (document/yorkie-event.controller.ts:41-75), the auth webhook is (key, verb) only (yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29-31), and no Yorkie document schema is registered. Every call site of mergeBudgetError/mergeBudgetAdmits in the repo is a writer (backend worksheet-settings.ts:127/163/178, yorkie-store.ts:1019, sheet.ts:2725/4891, xlsx-importer.ts:250-269). So a lower-trust rw principal (invited or share-link editor) writing oversized merge spans directly via the Yorkie SDK permanently hangs every other collaborator's open, including the workspace owner's — an unvalidated-untrusted-input availability break that crosses principals, not merely a local correctness bug.

verdict.reason: The absence is factually true — parseHidden's arr() (worksheet-settings.ts:79-87) range-checks each element but never the array length, and the spec (worksheet-settings.spec.ts:29-58) has no length case. But it is not blocking under the Security rubric. (a) The route is gated: worksheet.controller.ts:60-61 applies CombinedAuthGuard + WorkspaceScopeGuard + ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard, so only a principal already holding document write scope can reach PUT hidden (worksheet.controller.ts:160-181). (b) Unlike the merges case the diff bounded, there is no amplification: Sheet.loadHiddenState (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:621-632) just inserts each index into a Set, O(n), and readers are Set.has (sheet.ts:1884,1891) — nothing expands a product the way rebuildMergeCoverMap does for rs*cs, which is precisely why merges needed mergeBudgetError. (c) Because consumption is linear in body bytes, the existing bodyParser 25MB cap (main.ts:20,48-57) plus the per-element grid range check are already the effective ceiling, and Yorkie's per-document size limit (documented at packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/csv-doc-size.test.ts:10-21) rolls back anything near the top of that range at doc.update() time. (d) The write wholesale-replaces the field and causes no load-time throw, so it is reversible and does not lock collaborators out. Net: an authenticated-only, non-amplifying, already-capped hardening nit — not auth bypass, secret exposure, injection, or a broken crypto check.
